en.p: As shown in the figure, there is a sector OAB with radius 1 and central angle $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$. Let H be the foot of the perpendicular from a point P on arc AB to segment OA, and let Q, R, S be the intersections of the bisector of $\angle\mathrm{OAP}$ with the three segments HP, OP, OB, respectively. When $\angle\mathrm{APH}=\theta$, let $f(\theta)$ be the area of triangle AQH and $g(\theta)$ the area of triangle PSR.
When $\displaystyle\lim_{\theta\to 0+}\frac{\theta^3\times g(\theta)}{f(\theta)}=k$, find the value of $100k$. (Here $0<\theta<\dfrac{\pi}{4}$.) [4 points]
